item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-R05-E017","status":"rejected","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt concerns pre-departure and migration counselling offices, labour-office oversight, and other migration services; it does not contain the claimed company lists or figures."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-R05-E018","status":"rejected","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt discusses identity-document offices, banking, flights, and Egypt-EU cooperation, but does not mention the Egyptian-German centre, THAMM, or the claimed training and reintegration measures."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-R05-E019","status":"rejected","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt concerns consular assistance, passports, labour disputes, and other services; it does not support the claimed legal right to stand for election and vote or an electoral-list quota."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-R05-E020","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The report states that between January 2020 and October 2023, 1,884 cases arose concerning criminal networks involved in irregular migration and trafficking, including 1,194 irregular-migration cases and 654 human-trafficking cases. Up to 30 September 2023, the State Prosecution Office launched investigations into 67 incidents constituting human trafficking, including 20 sexual-exploitation cases, 27 forced-labour cases, and 20 other-exploitation cases.","notes":["Narrowed 'authorities recorded' to the excerpt's wording that cases 'arose' and that the State Prosecution Office launched investigations.","The excerpt reports the figures but does not establish convictions, remedies, or personal presidential direction."]}]}
